text: Healthcare Knowledge Centre Mental Health Clear, practical information about anxiety, stress, low mood, burnout and the role of general practice in mental healthcare. Find a guide Understanding Mental Health Mental health is part of whole-person healthcare. General practice can provide a confidential starting point for discussing changes in mood, anxiety, sleep, stress, functioning or wellbeing, and can coordinate further support when needed. Patients from Woolloongabba, East Brisbane and nearby inner-south communities can start with a GP when they are unsure what kind of mental health support may be appropriate. title: ADHD Assessment Pathways
description: Questions about ADHD may begin with difficulties at school, work or home.
headings: When Should I Seek Medical Advice?
text: Healthcare Knowledge Centre · ADHD & Neurodiversity ADHD Assessment Pathways Questions about ADHD may begin with difficulties at school, work or home. Assessment is a process that considers developmental history, functioning and other possible explanations for symptoms. Patient education Australian primary-care context Introduction Questions about ADHD may begin with difficulties at school, work or home. Assessment is a process that considers developmental history, functioning and other possible explanations for symptoms. What Is It? ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition associated with patterns of inattention and/or hyperactivity and impulsivity that affect everyday life. Diagnosis is not made from a single online quiz or a short symptom checklist. Australian assessment pathways vary by age, professional scope and service availability. Persistent inattention since childhood Difficulty across several settings Questions about specialist assessment Should I Be Concerned? Talk to a GP if longstanding attention, organisation or impulsivity difficulties affect daily functioning. Similar symptoms can arise from poor sleep, anxiety, depression, trauma or other health conditions, which should be considered during assessment. When Should I Seek Medical Advice? A concern about ADHD is usually not an emergency. If someone is in immediate danger, severely distressed or unable to stay safe, call 000 or seek emergency mental health assistance. How Can a GP Help? A GP can discuss the history, review physical and mental health, explain referral options and support interim strategies. Diagnosis and medicine decisions depend on an appropriately qualified clinician and current Queensland requirements; a GP consultation does not guarantee a diagnosis, prescription or referral acceptance. Specific examples of difficulties at school, home or work and any earlier reports may help clarify referral needs. If unsure which appointment to choose, call reception on (07) 3217 3344. Frequently Asked Questions Can an online ADHD test diagnose me? No. Screening tools can suggest discussing concerns with a clinician but cannot establish a diagnosis. Will I be diagnosed at my first GP visit? Usually not. The first appointment may clarify concerns and referral needs; a comprehensive assessment generally requires more information. description: Many people experience distraction or restlessness.
headings: When Should I Seek Medical Advice?
keywords: knowledge articles when should i seek adhd assessment
text: Healthcare Knowledge Centre · ADHD & Neurodiversity When Should I Seek ADHD Assessment? Many people experience distraction or restlessness. An assessment may be helpful when these difficulties have been persistent, have a developmental history and are significantly affecting everyday life. Patient education Australian primary-care context Introduction Many people experience distraction or restlessness. An assessment may be helpful when these difficulties have been persistent, have a developmental history and are significantly affecting everyday life. What Is It? ADHD symptoms may look different in children and adults. Examples include difficulties organising tasks, completing work, waiting, controlling impulses or managing competing demands. Sleep problems, anxiety and learning difficulties can overlap with ADHD symptoms. Longstanding organisational difficulties Symptoms affecting school, work or relationships Uncertainty about ADHD versus other conditions Should I Be Concerned? Consider a GP appointment if difficulties affect school, employment, relationships or self-care across more than one setting, particularly where there is evidence they began in childhood. In children, feedback from family and educators may be useful. When Should I Seek Medical Advice? Immediate risks to safety, self-harm concerns or severe behavioural crises warrant urgent support; call 000 for immediate danger. Routine ADHD assessment is not a crisis service. How Can a GP Help? A GP can explore symptom history, medical and mental health considerations, and whether assessment through a paediatrician, psychiatrist, psychologist or other appropriately qualified professional is suitable. Referral choice and costs should be discussed. Specific examples of difficulties at school, home or work and any earlier reports may help clarify referral needs. If unsure which appointment to choose, call reception on (07) 3217 3344. Frequently Asked Questions Can adults be assessed for ADHD? Yes. Adult assessment considers current functioning and evidence of symptoms beginning in childhood. Is difficulty concentrating always ADHD? No. Sleep, mood, medicines, stress and health conditions can produce similar difficulties. Trusted Australian Resources These Australian resources offer further general information. Recommendations and eligibility can change; your GP can explain how guidance applies to you. title: Understanding ADHD Referrals
description: A referral is a practical step towards assessment, not a confirmation that someone has ADHD.
headings: When Should I Seek Medical Advice?
text: Healthcare Knowledge Centre · ADHD & Neurodiversity Understanding ADHD Referrals A referral is a practical step towards assessment, not a confirmation that someone has ADHD. Understanding what information may be required can help you prepare. Patient education Australian primary-care context Introduction A referral is a practical step towards assessment, not a confirmation that someone has ADHD. Understanding what information may be required can help you prepare. What Is It? Specialist pathways differ for children and adults and may involve paediatrics, psychiatry or psychology. Availability, public or private options, costs and the professional permitted to diagnose or prescribe medicines are not identical across services. Preparing assessment history and records Questions about referral costs Co-occurring anxiety, sleep or learning issues Should I Be Concerned? Book a GP appointment if you need to discuss an assessment referral, an existing report or co-occurring sleep and mental health problems. Bringing school reports, previous assessments and details of daily difficulties may be helpful, but missing childhood paperwork should not prevent an initial discussion. When Should I Seek Medical Advice? Referral delays can be difficult. If mental health or safety deteriorates, seek timely support separately; call 000 for imminent danger. A routine specialist waiting list should not delay urgent assessment of new symptoms. How Can a GP Help? A GP can help select a suitable pathway, write relevant clinical information, assess other conditions and offer ongoing general healthcare. Specific prescribing and assessment arrangements depend on the clinician and current regulations; no booking guarantees a stimulant prescription. Specific examples of difficulties at school, home or work and any earlier reports may help clarify referral needs. If unsure which appointment to choose, call reception on (07) 3217 3344. Frequently Asked Questions Does a GP referral guarantee an appointment? No. Specialist services have different acceptance criteria, availability and fees. Confirm these with the provider. Can a psychologist assess ADHD? Some appropriately trained psychologists provide diagnostic assessment, but prescribing rights differ. Ask your GP which pathway fits your needs.
